SMTO-HTTP-0073 — A request setting has a value SMTO can't use

GUID: 6b6887f5-e855-43db-87c2-85f606740060
Slug: http-option-invalid
Domain: HTTP · Subsystem: http

What happened

  • One of the settings for a web request, such as how long to wait or how large a reply to accept, was outside what SMTO allows. Nothing was sent to the service.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In the conversation, ask SMTO to resend the request without a custom wait time or reply size limit. SMTO's normal values are always within the allowed range.
  2. If you need a longer wait, keep it at 2 minutes or less. If the reply is large, ask SMTO to save the reply as a file instead of showing it. A single request can wait at most 2 minutes, and a saved reply may be larger than one shown in the conversation.
  3. If it stops again, select Copy error details in this panel. The details name the exact setting that was out of range.

What success looks like

  • The request is sent and the step shows the service's reply.

If it still fails

  • Send the copied error details to the person who manages SMTO. Changing other timeouts in Settings won't help; this limit belongs to the web request itself.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • prepare_request rejected the request because timeout_seconds, max_response_bytes, response_mode, follow_redirects or refresh_observation has an invalid type or out-of-range value.

What this means

  • Timeout, max_response_bytes, response_mode, follow_redirects or refresh_observation fails the allowed exact types, values or numeric ranges. The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.

Why this can happen

  • Timeout, max_response_bytes, response_mode, follow_redirects or refresh_observation fails the allowed exact types, values or numeric ranges.

How to diagnose it

  • Check timeout 1–120 seconds and mode-specific byte bounds in the advertised contract; booleans must be actual booleans.

How to fix it

  • Use timeout_seconds 1-120, an integer max_response_bytes from 1 to 2 MiB inline (8 MiB with response_mode=artifact), response_mode inline or artifact, and real booleans for follow_redirects and refresh_observation (see prepare_request in gateway_core/http_contract.py). Shell timeouts and model context settings do not change these limits.
  • Use the types and bounds in the native HTTP tool contract. A shell timeout or model context setting does not change these request options.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • All options validate within the selected inline/artifact response contract.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
